tasks.short: Notation rule checking ported from s1kd check_brex_notation_rules
tasks.details: Implement notation rule checking (category A3). Port check_brex_notation_rules / check_entity: read NOTATION declarations from the internal DTD subset, accept a notation if some notationRule names it with @allowedNotationFlag != "0", and report the objectUse of the first inclusion rule otherwise. Requires parsing with DTD loading enabled. Implemented as BrexChecker._check_notation_rules / _check_entity_notation / _get_notation_rules_group in acd/brex_checker.py; results land in result["notations"] and feed _append_summary. Follows the C original in walking ENTITY declarations of the internal DTD subset (unparsed/NDATA entities specifically) rather than <!NOTATION> declarations directly, since that is what check_entity's entity->content actually reads; the internal DTD subset is available from lxml's default parser with no special DTD-loading options needed (it is inline in the document, unlike an external subset).

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: brDecisionIdentNumber captured and reported on every violation
tasks.details: Capture and report brDecisionRef/@brDecisionIdentNumber (category A5) on every violation — 262 rules in these three BREX carry one, and it is the identifier customers quote. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _show_rules reads the brDecisionRef sibling of objectPath/objectUse (confirmed against the real ATABREX evidence file, e.g. SOR-230 at line 773 of DMC-ATABREX-F-00-00-00-00A-022A-D_004-00_EN-US.XML) and carries its brDecisionIdentNumber (or None when absent) into every rule dict; _check_object_flag_0/1/2 add it to each violation record under BrDecisionIdentNumber, and the three xpathError diagnostics carry it too so a malformed rule can still be traced back to its decision number. Matches the C original, which only wires brDecisionRef into check_brex_rules (structure-object-rule checks) — SNS and notation-rule violations have no associated brDecisionRef in the schema and are unaffected. Covered by tests/test_br_decision_ref.py.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Business-rule severity levels from @brSeverityLevel and .brseveritylevels
tasks.details: Implement business-rule severity levels (category A6). Read structureObjectRule/@brSeverityLevel, fall back to brex/@defaultBrSeverityLevel, resolve against a .brseveritylevels file (<brSeverityLevels><brSeverityLevel value="brsl01" fail="yes">Error</brSeverityLevel>…), and let fail="no" levels report as warnings that do not fail the run. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _show_rules reads structureObjectRule/@brSeverityLevel (falling back to the brex root's @defaultBrSeverityLevel when absent) into each rule dict's brSeverityLevel key; set_severity_levels_path / _get_severity_levels load and cache a .brseveritylevels file into a {value: {fail, type}} table; _is_severity_failure ports is_failure (s1kd-brexcheck.c:569-605) — a violation fails unless a severity-levels file is set, defines that exact value, and marks it fail="no". _check_object_flag_0/1/2 attach BrSeverityLevel and Fail to every violation record, and _append_summary excludes Fail: False entries from the error count, reporting them instead as "N Errors, M Warnings" (unchanged "N Errors" format when there are no warnings, so existing callers/tests are unaffected). No explicit path defaults to the old always-fail behaviour, matching the C original when no -w flag is given. Covered by tests/test_severity_levels.py. Parent-directory auto-discovery of .brseveritylevels is the next task item, not part of this one.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: .brseveritylevels searched in parent directories, with an override parameter
tasks.details: Search parent directories for .brseveritylevels by default, with an override parameter. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _find_severity_levels_file walks from the checked XML's directory upward through its parents (adapting find_config, s1kd_tools.c:30-56, to search from the file's directory instead of the process's cwd) looking for a file named .brseveritylevels, returning the first match or None at the filesystem root. _get_severity_levels now falls back to this search whenever set_severity_levels_path has not been called explicitly. Two override paths: set_severity_levels_path (explicit file, unchanged, takes precedence and skips the search) and the new set_severity_levels_search(enabled: bool) (turns the default search off entirely, e.g. to ignore a discoverable file). Covered by new cases in tests/test_severity_levels.py: discovery in the XML's own directory, discovery in an ancestor directory, explicit-path precedence over an auto-discovered file, and search disabled ignoring a discoverable file; the two pre-existing "no severity levels" tests now call set_severity_levels_search(False) so they no longer depend on the ambient filesystem lacking a stray .brseveritylevels above the pytest temp dir.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: objectValue checking applied to every rule with objectValue children, not only flag 2
tasks.details: Apply objectValue checking to every rule that has objectValue children, not only flag 2 (s1kd is_invalid → check_objects_values). Ref §3.8. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: extracted the per-element value-matching loop out of _check_object_flag_2 into a shared _check_object_values(value, elements) helper (port of check_objects_values, s1kd-brexcheck.c:275-304), then wired it into _check_object_flag_1 — when a flag-1 rule's node-set is non-empty (the presence check passed) and the rule carries values_allowed/regex_allowed/ranges_allowed, its matched nodes are now also value-checked, with any failures appended to the '2' violation bucket. Flag 0 is intentionally left unchanged: per the C reference, check_objects_values is only reached when the node-set is non-empty, and a non-violating flag-0 rule always has an *empty* node-set (a non-empty one is already a presence violation), so there is nothing to value-check there.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: BREX resolution uses brexDmRef instead of the first dmRef with infoCode 022
tasks.details: Use brexDmRef for BREX resolution. Add a dedicated lookup for //brexDmRef|//brexref instead of "first dmRef with infoCode 022". Ref §3.7. Implemented in acd/s1000d.py: get_brex_ref now parses the object and runs the XPath //brexDmRef|//brexref (matching s1kd-brexcheck's find_brex_fname_from_doc) to get the one node that actually carries the applicable-BREX reference, then reads its nested .//dmCode|.//avee (plus .//issueInfo for the 4.0+ form) instead of scanning every dmRef/refdm in the document for infoCode/incode 022. Verified against the real ATA CMP evidence base (DMC-CTTAE29N-A-00-00-00-01A-00KA-D... → DMC-ATABREX-...-01A-... → DMC-ATABREX-...-00A-... → DMC-S1000D-F-04-10-0301-00A-022A-D, the last self-referencing to terminate the chain) — identical, correct resolution before and after the change. Covered by tests/test_brex_dm_ref_resolution.py, including a case with a decoy dmRef (infoCode="022", pointing at a nonexistent DM) placed before the real brexDmRef in document order: confirmed by inlining the old scan-based logic that it would have followed the decoy and raised NoBrexDefined, while the new lookup resolves and checks the real BREX. The legacy S1000D <= 3.0 brexref/avee form is also covered. The pre-existing _init_brex_list cycle-guard/None-handling gap (next task item) is unchanged.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Cycle guard in the layered-BREX walk; a missing BREX reference no longer raises
tasks.details: Add a visited-set cycle guard to the layered-BREX walk in _init_brex_list, and handle get_brex_ref returning None without a TypeError. Ref §3.7.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Built-in default BREX modules shipped, with a default-BREX-only mode and fallback
tasks.details: Ship the built-in default BREX modules (s1kd-tools/tools/s1kd-brexcheck/brex/, issues A/D/E/F/G/H plus DMC-AE-A-…) and add a "check against default BREX only" mode equivalent to s1kd-brexcheck -B, plus the fallback when the referenced BREX cannot be found. Implemented as a new acd/default_brex.py module plus the 7 bundled BREX XML files under acd/brex/ (shipped as package data via pyproject.toml), ported from s1kd-brexcheck's brex/, default_brex_dmc, search_brex_fname_from_default_brex and load_brex (s1kd-brexcheck.c): default_brex_dmc(schema) selects the schema-appropriate built-in BREX by the same substring rules as the C original (so e.g. S1000D_4-0-1/S1000D_4-0-2 sub-issues still match S1000D_4-0), default_brex_path(logical_dmc) resolves one of the 7 logical DMCs to its bundled file path, and find_default_brex_fallback(ref) matches a BREX reference against the 7 built-ins by base DMC plus issue/inWork (accepting any issue when the reference does not specify one). BrexChecker.use_default_brex(enabled=True) in acd/brex_checker.py is the -B/--default-brex equivalent: _init_brex_list short-circuits to the single schema-selected built-in BREX, ignoring any brexDmRef/brexref and skipping layering entirely, matching the C original's -B behaviour. The fallback is wired into _init_brex_list's existing brexDmRef walk (collapsed from two dead-duplicate branches into one while making this change, since branch two's guard was provably unreachable): when find_document_by_reference fails to locate a referenced BREX, find_default_brex_fallback is tried before giving up, at every layer of the chain (not just the top-level reference), exactly as find_brex_fname_from_doc is used uniformly in the C original. Per explicit product decision, the fallback is not silent like the C tool (which only logs when the fallback also fails) — every substitution is recorded in the result dict's new always-present brexFallback list (Reference, UsedBuiltinBrex, BuiltinBrexPath per entry), which _append_summary excludes from the error/warning count as purely informational. override_brex_list/use_default_brex reset _brex_fallbacks so stale markers never leak across runs or directory-mode files. Verified end-to-end against the real bundled files (not just fixtures): schema selection for all 7 built-ins resolves to an existing file, use_default_brex() checks a legacy S1000D 3.0 object against the real bundled DMC-AE-A-... BREX and ignores an unrelated brexDmRef, and a brexDmRef naming DMC-AE-A-... that can't be found on disk falls back to the real bundled copy (which self-references to terminate the layering walk, confirming the existing self-reference guard still applies to a fallback-resolved file) and is flagged in brexFallback; a reference to neither an on-disk nor a built-in BREX still raises NoBrexDefined unchanged. Covered by tests/test_default_brex.py.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Multiple BREX search paths and recursive search (-I, -r)
tasks.details: Add multiple BREX search paths and recursive search (-I, -r equivalents) alongside the current single set_brex_path. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: add_brex_search_path(path) appends a directory to a new _brex_search_paths list (the -I/--include equivalent, repeatable), clear_brex_search_paths() resets it, and set_brex_recursive_search(enabled) toggles a new _brex_recursive_search flag (the -r/--recursive equivalent) that applies uniformly to the primary path and every added search path, mirroring the C original's find_csdb_object(..., recursive_search) calls for search_dir and each spaths[i] (s1kd-brexcheck.c:538-547). _init_brex_list's resolution loop now tries self._brex_dir_path[0] first and, only if that misses, walks _brex_search_paths in the order added, stopping at the first match, before falling back to the built-in default BREX as before. acd/s1000d.py's find_document_by_reference gained a recursive: bool = True parameter (default preserves the pre-existing always-recursive os.walk behaviour; False restricts the search to files directly inside the given directory, via os.listdir). Covered by tests/test_brex_search_paths.py: search-path fallback and ordering, rejecting a non-directory path, clearing search paths, recursive-on-by-default vs. recursive-off for both the primary path and an added search path, and direct unit tests of find_document_by_reference's recursive parameter.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: S1000D <= 3.0 legacy BREX spellings supported
tasks.details: Support S1000D <= 3.0 legacy BREX spellings (category C5): objpath / objuse / objval, @objappl, @val1 / @val2, contextrules/@context. s1kd accepts all of these; we accept none. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _get_object_rule_nodes now also collects //structrules/objrule/objpath alongside the modern //structureObjectRuleGroup/structureObjectRule/objectPath -- the real S1000D <= 3.0 default BREX nests rules exactly three levels below contextrules (objpath -> objrule -> structrules -> contextrules), same depth as the modern schema below contextRules, so the existing fixed-depth getparent().getparent().getparent() walk in _show_rules needed no change, just an @rulesContext|@context fallback lookup. _show_rules reads objectUse|objuse, @allowedObjectFlag|@objappl, and objectValue|objval with @valueForm|@valtype plus @valueAllowed|@val1[~@val2] (port of get_value_allowed, s1kd-brexcheck.c:194-216, which concatenates val1/val2 into the same first~last string our is_in_set already parses). _check_rules's dispatch loop now also routes a rule whose flag is entirely absent into the flag-2 value-check path whenever it carries objval children -- the shape of the great majority of rules in the real S1000D 3.0 default BREX (e.g. //@accpnltype, no @objappl at all) -- matching s1kd's is_invalid (s1kd-brexcheck.c:307-331), which falls through to check_objects_values whenever allowedObjectFlag is NULL. Verified end-to-end against the real bundled acd/brex/DMC-AE-A-04-10-0301-00A-022A-D_003-00.XML (the actual S1000D <= 3.0 default BREX shipped with s1kd-brexcheck), not just hand-built fixtures. Covered by tests/test_legacy_brex_spellings.py: flag 0/1/2 violations under legacy spelling, a flag-less value-only rule, range and pattern valtypes, a rule with no objval children never being a violation, contextrules/@context schema-qualification correctly skipping a non-matching object, a no-false-positives case with valid values, and the real bundled default BREX checked end-to-end against both a violating and a conforming object.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Rules selected with the descendant axis and filtered by rulesContext at selection
tasks.details: Select rules with the descendant axis and filter at selection time, matching //contextRules[not(@rulesContext) or @rulesContext=$schema]//structureObjectRule, and stop walking parents by fixed depth. Also removes the lxml FutureWarning. Ref §3.6. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _get_object_rule_nodes now takes an optional schema and selects with Element.xpath() (real XPath via libxml2) instead of findall() (the restricted ElementPath dialect, whose leading // on a parsed tree is what raised the "This search incorrectly ignores the root element" FutureWarning), using the descendant axis //contextRules[not(@rulesContext) or @rulesContext=$schema]//structureObjectRule/objectPath with $schema bound as an XPath variable so only unqualified or schema-matching rules are selected at all, regardless of how deeply structureObjectRule is nested under contextRules. The S1000D <= 3.0 spelling gets the equivalent treatment: //contextrules[not(@context) or @context=$schema]//objrule/objpath. _show_rules threads schema through from its caller (_check_rules, which already had it from get_schema_from_xml) and, since the enclosing contextRules/contextrules element is no longer guaranteed to sit exactly three getparent() calls up, finds it with next(x.iterancestors('contextRules', 'contextrules'), None) instead — correct at any nesting depth, and a None result (no such ancestor) degrades to an empty contextRules rather than raising. Verified: full suite passes with -W error::FutureWarning, confirming the warning is gone; the existing _check_object_flag_0/1/2 schema-equality checks stay in place as a harmless no-op now that filtering already happened at selection.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Every namespace in scope at the objectPath node registered
tasks.details: Register every namespace in scope at the objectPath node rather than a hard-coded rdf + xsi dictionary. Ref §3.12. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _show_rules now captures x.nsmap (lxml's full in-scope namespace map, walking every ancestor up to the BREX root, not just a fixed depth) for each objectPath/objpath node, remaps the lxml default-namespace key None to '' as elementpath expects, and stores it per-rule as value['namespaces'] layered over NS_DICT as a base (so the well-known rdf/xsi prefixes stay resolvable even when a BREX declares neither). _check_object_flag_0/1/2 now construct their elementpath.Selector with value.get('namespaces', NS_DICT) instead of the module-level constant, and the Saxon path in _check_object_flag_0 declares each rule's namespaces (skipping the empty/default prefix, which PyXdmNode.declare_namespace does not accept) instead of iterating NS_DICT. NS_DICT itself is unchanged and still exported from acd/__init__.py for backward compatibility. Covered by tests/test_objectpath_namespaces.py: a prefix declared only on the BREX root resolves at a deeply nested objectPath, a prefix declared only on one structureObjectRule resolves for that rule and does not leak into a sibling rule's namespace map, rdf/xsi still resolve with no local declaration, and a direct check of _show_rules's per-rule namespaces dict.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: remove-deleted support: changeType="delete" elements dropped before checking
tasks.details: Add remove-deleted support (-^): drop elements with @changeType="delete" before checking. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _remove_deleted_elements ports rem_delete_nodes/rem_delete_elems (s1kd_tools.c:1054-1088) -- recursively unlinks any element whose @changeType (or legacy @change) attribute is "delete", without descending into a removed element's children (they go with it). _check_rules gained a remove_deleted: bool = False parameter; when set, it is applied to the parsed document right after parsing and before the schema-based SNS/notation/content-rule checks, matching the C original's ordering (rem_delete_elems runs once, immediately after parse, ahead of every subsequent check). Since nodes are removed in place on the already-parsed tree rather than by re-parsing, surviving elements keep their original .sourceline, so line numbers in violation records are unaffected. The Saxon path (_check_object_flag_0) previously always re-read self._xml_path from disk, which would have bypassed the in-memory removal; it now accepts an xml_text parameter and, when remove_deleted is active, _check_rules serialises the modified tree once and passes it through so Saxon evaluates the same reduced document as the elementpath path. validate() gained the matching remove_deleted parameter and threads it to _check_rules in both single-file and directory mode. Covered by tests/test_remove_deleted.py: a deleted element still flagged by default (opt-in only), the same element dropped from a flag-0 "must not be present" check once enabled, a non-deleted sibling still correctly flagged with the option on, the legacy @change="delete" spelling, a deleted parent taking its children with it, a flag-1 "must be present" rule that starts passing (element present) and starts failing (element removed) as the option is toggled, and the option threaded end-to-end through validate().

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Parser options: XInclude, entity resolution, XML catalogs, ignore-empty
tasks.details: Add parser options: XInclude processing, entity resolution, XML catalogs, and the ignore-empty behaviour for empty / non-XML inputs. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _build_xml_parser/_finish_parse/_parse_xml_file/_parse_xml_text build a single lxml XMLParser from the checker's parser-option state and apply XInclude processing afterwards, and now back every internal parse of the checked object and every BREX file (_check_rules, _get_object_rule_nodes, _get_sns_rules_group, _get_notation_rules_group) instead of ad hoc etree.parse(...) calls -- mirroring read_xml_doc (s1kd_tools.c:532-543), which applies DEFAULT_PARSE_OPTS uniformly to every CSDB object it reads. set_xinclude(enabled) is the --xinclude equivalent (ElementTree.xinclude(), mirroring xmlXIncludeProcessFlags). set_resolve_entities(enabled) controls lxml's resolve_entities parser flag (--noent); set_entity_resolution(load_external_dtd, allow_network) is the --dtdload/--net pair, off by default so parsing a checked object cannot trigger unexpected file/network access on its own -- verified that an external-DTD-declared entity raises XMLSyntaxError by default and resolves once load_external_dtd=True is set (entities declared directly in the internal DTD subset, even via a SYSTEM identifier, were already resolved regardless, since that is a document-supplied declaration rather than a fetched external subset). set_xml_catalog(path) is the --xml-catalog <file> equivalent; since lxml has no catalog-loading binding, it appends to the XML_CATALOG_FILES environment variable, which libxml2 reads on its first catalog lookup (documented caveat: only takes effect if set before that first lookup in the process). set_ignore_empty(enabled) is -e/--ignore-empty: _is_valid_xml_file attempts a real parse and validate() uses it to skip an empty/non-XML object before _init_brex_list()/_check_rules() ever run -- left out of the results mapping entirely in directory mode (matching s1kd-brexcheck's continue), reported as {"Skipped": True, "Summary": "..."} for a single object. Covered by tests/test_parser_options.py: XInclude on/off, external-DTD entity resolution on/off, the network-access-requires-dtd-loading guard, XML catalog registration/dedup/missing-file rejection, and ignore-empty for both single-file and directory mode with and without the flag set.

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Violations carry the node's canonical XPath and a copy of the violating subtree
tasks.details: Emit the node's canonical XPath and a copy of the violating subtree in each violation record (categories D2, D3), shallow by default with an opt-in deep copy. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _select_with_nodes re-implements the value-extraction step elementpath's own Selector.select performs (XPathToken.get_results), but from the lower-level, un-formatted root_token.select(), so it can return the raw XPath node backing each node-set item alongside the same formatted result .select() would give -- the formatted API alone discards an attribute/text result's parent element entirely, which is what dump_nodes_xml (s1kd-brexcheck.c:334-360) needs to report a node's canonical XPath and copy it. _node_xpath_and_copy reads the node's extended_path (elementpath's own canonical-path computation, e.g. /dml[1]/forbiddenElement[2] or /dml[1]/someElement[1]/@constrainedAttr) and, for an attribute/text result, copies its owning element instead of the bare value (if (node->type == XML_ATTRIBUTE_NODE) node = node->parent; in the C original) -- shallow by default (tag and attributes only, matching xmlCopyNode(node, 2)), or the full recursive subtree when a new deep_copy_nodes parameter (the -8/--deep-copy-nodes equivalent) is enabled, threaded through validate() -> _check_rules() -> _check_object_flag_0/1/2 / _check_object_values. Every content-rule violation record (flags 0, 1, 2) now carries NodeXpath and Object (an XML string, None when no node backs the violation, e.g. a flag-1 "required but missing" violation or a boolean-valued flag-0 rule). The Saxon path (_check_object_flag_0's self._saxon branch) is left emitting None for both fields, consistent with its existing acknowledged incompleteness (§3.12, "Make the Saxon path complete or remove it"). Covered by tests/test_node_xpath_and_copy.py: canonical XPath and shallow copy for a repeated element violation (positional indices [1]/[2]), deep copy including descendants and tail text, an attribute violation resolving to its owning element, None/None for a missing-element flag-1 violation and a boolean flag-0 rule, and deep_copy_nodes threaded end-to-end through validate().

tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Real line numbers taken from the parsed tree
tasks.details: Report the violating node's real line number from the parsed tree instead of scanning raw text for the attribute name. Ref §3.12, category D1. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: extracted the element-resolution half of _node_xpath_and_copy (walking a raw _select_with_nodes XPath node to its owning lxml element -- itself for an element result, the parent for an attribute/text result) into a shared _resolve_owning_element(node) helper, and added _node_line_number(node) on top of it that reads the owning element's .sourceline (lxml's binding to libxml2's xmlGetLineNo, matching what s1kd-brexcheck reports). _check_object_flag_0's element/attribute branch and _check_object_values (shared by flags 1/2) now call _node_line_number(nodes[idx]) instead of the old element.sourceline attempt with a text-scan-for-the-attribute-name fallback on AttributeError -- that fallback matched the *first* line in the file containing the attribute name, so it silently misreported the line for every violation past the first repeated attribute/element in a document, and only handled attributes, never element or text-node results without a direct .sourceline. Fixed to "x" only when a violation has no backing node at all (a boolean-valued flag-0 rule, or a flag-1 "required but missing" result). The Saxon path (_check_object_flag_0's self._saxon branch) still text-scans via regex_builder, matching its existing acknowledged incompleteness ("Make the Saxon path complete or remove it", §3.12/§4.4). Covered by tests/test_violation_line_numbers.py: multiple forbiddenElement violations resolve to their own distinct real lines rather than all collapsing to the first occurrence, repeated-attribute violations resolve to each owning element's real line, an element-text value violation resolves correctly, and Line is a real int rather than a string.

tasks.short: XML report compatible with s1kd-brexcheck -x
tasks.details: Add an XML report output compatible with the s1kd-brexcheck -x shape (brexCheck/document/brex/error/{brDecisionRef,objectPath,objectUse,object}) so existing tooling can consume our output (category D6). Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: to_xml_report(result) converts a validate() result (single-object or directory-mode) into a <brexCheck> document tree matching the C tool's shape (document[@path]/{sns,notations,brex[@path]/{error,xpathError}}), ported piecewise from the relevant s1kd-brexcheck.c fragments -- _append_error_node from the <error> construction in check_brex_rules (s1kd-brexcheck.c:900-938, including its brSeverityLevel/fail attribute logic), _append_sns_notation_nodes from check_brex_sns_rules (s1kd-brexcheck.c:1077-1134) and check_brex_notation_rules (s1kd-brexcheck.c:1213-1224). tasks.group: 4.2 P1 — Rule categories we do not check but s1kd-brexcheck does
tasks.short: Formatted Excel and HTML reports
tasks.details: Add formatted Excel and HTML reports for human readers, alongside the machine-readable JSON and -x-compatible XML ones (category D6). Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: to_excel_report(result, path) writes a styled .xlsx workbook (openpyxl, imported inside the method so importing brex_checker stays cheap and the dependency is only needed by callers who actually want a workbook) and to_html_report(result, path=None, title=...) returns -- and optionally writes -- a self-contained HTML document. Both accept either result shape (single object after set_xml, batch/folder after set_xml_dir, distinguished by _is_single_object_result like every other report) and are built from the same shared, render-ready helpers so they cannot drift apart or from the existing reports: _violation_records (one traversal pairing each BrexViolation with the raw record it came from -- violations() is now a projection of it, so the walk and its skip rules exist once), _report_violation_rows (the flat, column-keyed rows both renderers consume, duplicate=True entries excluded exactly as in run_summary/to_json_report/to_xml_report), _document_stats (per-document errors/warnings/status, the batch counterpart of run_summary's run totals), _xpath_error_rows (category D8 diagnostics -- rules that were silently *not* checked, already in the XML report as xpathError nodes) and the existing _json_document_sections for SNS/notation/nonContextRules/brexFallback content. The one thing these two carry that BrexViolation cannot is the raw record's Description, which for a flag-2 record is the only carrier of the value actually found ("Element/Attribute (X) did not match the object values.") -- surfaced as a Finding column rather than by widening the dataclass and changing the JSON report's shape. The workbook opens on a Summary sheet (run totals, violations by brSeverityLevel, and a per-document pass/fail table) followed by Violations, then SNS, Notations, XPath errors, Non-context rules and BREX fallback, each omitted when the run produced nothing of that kind; formatting is a coloured bold frozen header band with autofilter, borders and wrapped text on every cell, tuned column widths, zebra banding, rows tinted by outcome (red error / amber warning / green passing document) and coloured sheet tabs, with cell values sanitised of control characters and truncated well inside Excel's 32767-character limit for deep node copies (-8). The HTML report mirrors it: KPI cards, severity chips, the per-document table (batch runs only), a violations table with a live text filter and an errors-only switch, collapsible sections and <details>-wrapped node source. It follows the reader's prefers-color-scheme for dark/light with a toggle that overrides it in both directions (full light palette on bare :root, dark redefined under a :root:not([data-theme="light"])-guarded media query and again under :root[data-theme="dark"]), remembered in localStorage behind a try/catch so a file:// copy with site data blocked still renders, and pulls in nothing external at all -- CSS and JS inline, no fonts, images or CDN links -- so it survives being e-mailed or opened off a network share. Shared colours live in one _REPORT_PALETTE so a workbook and an HTML report of the same run read as the same document. Covered by tests/test_excel_report.py (sheet set for batch and single-object runs, one row per violation with severity/BR-decision/allowed-values/finding, the Summary sheet's totals and per-document table, header styling/freeze/autofilter, per-cell borders and wrapping, column widths, outcome tinting, long-snippet truncation, the conditional SNS and XPath-error sheets, omission of empty sheets, and an ignore-empty skipped-file run) and tests/test_html_report.py (complete document structure, batch and single-object content, summary cards and severity chips, found-vs-allowed rendering, the empty state for a clean run, escaping of markup in rule text and node snippets, writing to a path, a configurable title, the XPath-errors section, the dark/light contract, the filter controls, and the absence of any external reference).

tasks.short: Run summary: documents passed / failed and violations by severity
tasks.details: Add a run summary with documents passed/failed and violations by severity (category D7). Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: extracted the counting logic previously inline in _append_summary into a shared _count_violations(object_flag_dict) helper that returns (error_count, warning_count, severity_counts), tallying content-rule violations under their resolved BrSeverityLevel (or None when absent) and SNS/notation violations under None too (they have no severity-level concept at all, per §A6); _append_summary now calls it and is otherwise unchanged. run_summary(result) is the new port of s1kd-brexcheck -T/--totals: a separate, opt-in conversion over a finished validate() result -- the same pattern to_xml_report already uses -- rather than being folded into validate() itself, so validate()'s return shape is unchanged for existing callers. It accepts either a single-object or directory-mode result (via _is_single_object_result, same as to_xml_report) and returns {DocumentsChecked, DocumentsPassed, DocumentsFailed, DocumentsSkipped, Errors, Warnings, ViolationsBySeverity}; a document "passes" when its error count (warnings from fail="no" severities excluded) is zero. Noted limitation: directory-mode validate() drops a skipped file from its results mapping entirely (continue) rather than recording a Skipped marker, so DocumentsSkipped can only ever reflect single-object mode's skip path -- fixing that would mean changing validate()'s directory-mode contract, out of scope here. to_xml_report gained a new _append_run_summary_node that prepends a <summary documentsChecked=... documentsPassed=... documentsFailed=... documentsSkipped=... errors=... warnings=...><severity value="..." count=".../></summary> node (built from run_summary, so the two never disagree) as the first child of <brexCheck> -- an addition beyond the C tool's -x shape, since s1kd-brexcheck's totals are -T-only console output with no XML report equivalent. Covered by tests/test_run_summary.py: a passing document, a failing document with severity tallied, a warning-only document that still passes, SNS/notation violations counted as errors with no severity, directory-mode aggregation across documents, a skipped document counted separately, and the XML report's <summary> node matching run_summary()'s counts.

tasks.short: nonContextRules surfaced as informational report entries
tasks.details: Surface nonContextRules/nonContextRule (category A4) in the report as informational entries — text plus brDecisionRef — so authors see the human-readable business rules that apply. They are not machine-checkable, but silently dropping them hides a whole rule class. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _get_non_context_rules collects every nonContextRules/nonContextRule from each BREX in the active chain (self._brex_list[0]), reading its brDecisionRef/@brDecisionIdentNumber (None when absent) and its text -- from the simplePara child the real S1000D default BREX uses, with a full-itertext() fallback for a nonContextRule with no simplePara wrapper. Wired into _check_rules as a new, always-present result["nonContextRules"] key, populated unconditionally (like notations, not gated on dmodule roots the way sns is, since non-context rules describe the whole BREX, not a specific object). Purely informational, not a violation: _count_violations/_append_summary/run_summary all skip the key (it would otherwise crash the flag-0/1/2 counting loop, since its value is a list, not a per-flag dict), and to_xml_report gained _append_non_context_rules_node, which emits a <nonContextRules> node (one <nonContextRule> per entry, nesting a <brDecisionRef> and a <text>) only when the chain defines at least one -- omitted entirely otherwise, since (unlike sns/notations) there is no pass/fail state to report with a <noErrors/> counterpart. Verified against the real bundled default BREX (acd/brex/DMC-S1000D-H-04-10-0301-00A-022A-D_001-00_EN-US.XML), which correctly yields the one real nonContextRule ("Deletion of data modules is treated as a special case of update...", BREX-S1-00245) -- also present, in the same form, in the F issue; the E and G issues carry the equivalent rule with no brDecisionRef. Covered by tests/test_non_context_rules.py: text plus brDecisionRef extraction, a rule with no brDecisionRef, a rule with no simplePara wrapper, multiple rules in document order, no nonContextRules at all, non-effect on the error count, collection across a layered/multi-BREX chain, and the XML report node (present and omitted).

tasks.short: valueTailoring (lexical / restrictable) reported with each value violation
tasks.details: Report objectValue/@valueTailoring (category C4) with each value violation, distinguishing lexical (value list may be extended) from restrictable (value list may only be narrowed), so downstream tailoring review knows which allowed-value sets a project may legally change. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _show_rules now also collects a value_tailoring list alongside values_allowed/regex_allowed/ranges_allowed -- one {valueForm, valueAllowed, valueTailoring} entry per objectValue that actually declares @valueTailoring (absent on the S1000D <= 3.0 objval/val1 spelling, and on plenty of 4.x rules too -- 193 of 2462 in the evidence base -- so an undeclared value is left out rather than padded with a None entry, since there is nothing to distinguish for it). _check_object_values (shared by flag 2 and the flag-1-with-objectValue-children path, §3.8) attaches it to every value violation as 'ValueTailoring', alongside the existing 'Single Values'/'Pattern Values'/'Range Values' echo (D5) -- so a violation on a rule mixing tailoring policies (e.g. "aa" lexical, "bb" restrictable) reports both, distinguishable by looking up the failing rule's allowed values. Not wired into to_xml_report, matching the precedent already set there: to_xml_report's own task note records that echoing allowed values into the XML report was deliberately left out of scope, and adding ValueTailoring alone without its sibling value lists would be inconsistent. Verified against the real bundled default BREX (acd/brex/DMC-S1000D-H-04-10-0301-00A-022A-D_001-00_EN-US.XML): 84 rules carry declared tailoring, split 577 lexical / 796 restrictable across their objectValue children. Covered by tests/test_value_tailoring.py: a rule mixing lexical and restrictable values on the same violation, a rule with no declared tailoring reporting an empty list, pattern- and range-form values carrying tailoring, the flag-1 value-check path, and the legacy objval spelling (no valueTailoring concept, reports empty).

tasks.group: 4.3 P2 — Rule categories neither tool checks
tasks.short: Rules unreachable by rulesContext reported as BREX warnings
tasks.details: Detect rules made unreachable by rulesContext — e.g. a rulesContext naming a schema no object in the CSDB uses, or a typo'd schema URI. Report as a BREX warning. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py as BrexChecker._lint_unreachable_rules_context, wired into lint_brex(brex_path, csdb_schemas=None) as a new opt-in parameter: when given an iterable of schema URI strings actually used by the target CSDB, every contextRules/contextrules group whose rulesContext/context names a schema absent from that set is reported as an UnreachableRulesContext finding (one per distinct unreachable schema string, with every declaring group's line under Lines); an unqualified group is never flagged, since it always applies regardless of schema. A typo'd schema URI is indistinguishable from "legitimately declared for a schema this particular CSDB happens not to use" without a CSDB to compare against, so the check is skipped entirely (not "everything qualified is unreachable") when csdb_schemas is None (the default, so every existing lint_brex call site is unaffected) or empty. s1000d.collect_csdb_schemas(directory, recursive=True) is the new helper that builds this set for a caller: walks a CSDB directory (same recursive/non-recursive convention as find_document_by_reference) and collects the distinct xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation values via the existing get_schema_from_xml, tolerating an unreadable or non-well-formed file. Verified against the real evidence-base CSDB (CMP 21-77-05, 63 objects): collect_csdb_schemas correctly found the 10 schemas actually in use (this delivery uses the per-info-kind "strict" schema variant, not "flat"), and lint_brex on the real DMC-ATABREX-...-01A... correctly flagged the 8 rulesContext schemas the ATABREX declares rules for that no object in this particular delivery uses (fault.xsd, container.xsd, dml.xsd, checklist.xsd, crew.xsd, sb.xsd, schedul.xsd, wrngdata.xsd), with zero false positives against the 10 schemas that are in use. Covered by tests/test_brex_lint.py: an unreachable schema reported, a used schema not flagged, the check skipped without csdb_schemas, the check skipped when csdb_schemas is empty, and an unqualified group never flagged regardless of csdb_schemas.

tasks.group: 4.3 P2 — Rule categories neither tool checks
tasks.short: Per-rule hit statistics (evaluated / matched / violated)
tasks.details: Report per-rule hit statistics (rules evaluated / matched / violated) so a project can see which BREX rules never fire against its data set. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: self._rule_stats, keyed per distinct content rule by the new _rule_stat_key ((Brex, contextRules, xpath) — the same rule identity lint_brex's duplicate checks already treat as interchangeable), accumulates across every call to _check_rules — i.e. across an entire directory-mode validate() run, or across as many single-object validate() calls as a caller makes over a whole CSDB — since the feature is explicitly about visibility across a data set, not a single document; reset_rule_statistics() starts a fresh one, rule_hit_statistics() returns the accumulated list. _record_rule_evaluated is called once per rule per document from _check_rules's dispatch loop, before _check_object_flag_0/1/2, so a rule counts as evaluated even when it never reaches a check function at all (an allowedObjectFlag="2" rule with no objectValue children — the same silent no-op lint_brex's EmptyValueFlag2 finding already flags statically — now visibly stays at 0 matched / 0 violated forever at runtime too, confirming the static finding). _record_rule_hit(value, matched, violated) is called once per rule per document from inside _check_object_flag_0 (both the Saxon and elementpath paths), _check_object_flag_1 and _check_object_flag_2, reusing the selector result each function already computed (no extra XPath evaluation): matched means value['xpath'] located something in this document — a non-empty node-set or a true boolean result — independent of what allowedObjectFlag does with that outcome (a found forbidden node for flag 0, a found required node for flag 1, a found value-constrained node for flag 2); violated means this evaluation produced a violation, folding in a flag-1 rule's follow-on value check (§3.8) so its overall Violated reflects either a presence failure or a value failure. Neither is recorded on an xpathError (the selector never ran), though _record_rule_evaluated still counts that attempt. Scoped to content rules only, matching how the rest of the taxonomy (§2.A) separates categories — SNS and notation rules are checked as one pass per document, not rule-by-rule, so they have no per-rule breakdown here (verified: a real SNS violation surfaced during end-to-end testing below correctly did not appear in any rule's Violated count). Verified end-to-end against the real evidence-base chain (the 919-rule ATABREX-01A/00A/S1000D-default layering) by running validate() across 5 real data modules from CMP 21-77-05: 549 distinct rules tracked, with the per-document schema-qualification correctly reflected (474 of 549 evaluated in all 5 mixed-info-kind documents, the rest only in the subset whose schema they're qualified for), 13 matched at least once and 536 never matched against this small sample — exactly the "which rules never fire" signal the feature is for. Covered by tests/test_rule_hit_statistics.py: accumulation across two documents for flag 0 (never-present, sometimes-present), flag 1 (sometimes-required-and-present), flag 2 (matched-but-valid vs. matched-and-invalid), and a flag-2 rule with no objectValue staying at 0/0 forever; identifying fields carried on each stat; reset_rule_statistics clearing accumulated state; and an empty result before any check has run.

tasks.group: 4.3 P2 — Rule categories neither tool checks
tasks.short: Cross-BREX conflict detection for layered BREX
tasks.details: Add cross-BREX conflict detection for layered BREX — the same objectPath given contradictory allowedObjectFlags, or restrictable value sets widened by a lower layer. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py as BrexChecker.lint_brex_layers(entry_brex_path), a standalone opt-in method (no equivalent in s1kd-brexcheck) that resolves the same brexDmRef/brexref layer chain _init_brex_list would follow, but starting from a BREX file directly rather than from an object that references it — extracted the walk itself (resolution order, search-path fallback, built-in-BREX fallback, visited-set cycle guard) out of _init_brex_list into a new shared _walk_brex_chain(xml_start, search_dir) so both call sites share one implementation; _init_brex_list is otherwise behaviourally unchanged (confirmed by the full existing suite, including the cycle-guard and dead-end-chain tests in tests/test_brex_dm_ref_resolution.py, passing unmodified). Layer order follows official S1000D valueTailoring terminology: entry_brex_path (layer 0) is the "lower", project-specific BREX that may only restrict what a "higher", more general BREX further down the chain (ultimately a master/default BREX, at a larger layer index) declares. Two rules are compared as "the same rule" when they share both their rulesContext/context qualifier and exact objectPath/objpath text (reusing _show_rules per layer) — a documented simplification that does not catch an unqualified rule in one layer conflicting with a schema-qualified rule for the same path in another. Two findings: ConflictingAllowedObjectFlag, when the same rule is required absent ("0") by one layer and present ("1") by another — verified against the real ATABREX-01A/00A/S1000D-default chain that this is the *only* flag pair worth flagging: an initial version that flagged any two differing flags produced two false positives on that real chain (@commercialClassification, @caveat), each a project layer forbidding an attribute outright ("0") that a more general layer only value-constrains ("2") — a legitimate narrowing, not a conflict, since an absent attribute trivially satisfies a "value constrained if present" rule too; and RestrictableValueSetWidened, when the same rule declares a single-form objectValue with valueTailoring="restrictable" in two or more layers and a lower layer's allowed-value set is not a subset of a higher layer's set for that rule (pattern/range forms are not compared — a general regex/range subset relationship is out of scope). Verified against the real evidence-base chain (DMC-ATABREX-...-01A... -> ...-00A... -> DMC-S1000D-F-..., 919 rules combined): zero findings, confirming the refined flag-conflict logic and the value-widening check both correctly produce no false positives against real, well-maintained production data. Covered by tests/test_brex_layer_conflicts.py: a genuine "0"/"1" conflict detected with both layers identified, a "0"/"2" pairing correctly *not* flagged, restrictable value-set widening detected with the exact extra values reported, an agreeing rule across layers not flagged, and a single-layer BREX (no further brexDmRef) producing no findings.

tasks.group: 4.3 P2 — Rule categories neither tool checks
tasks.short: SNS rule tables validated (duplicate codes, missing titles, codes off pattern)
tasks.details: Validate SNS rule tables themselves (duplicate snsCode at a level, missing snsTitle, codes outside the pattern declared elsewhere in the BREX). Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py as BrexChecker._lint_sns_rules_table, wired unconditionally into lint_brex (no opt-in needed, unlike the CSDB-schema check above, since everything it needs is already in the one BREX file being linted): walks every snsSystem/snsSubSystem/snsSubSubSystem/snsAssy element the BREX declares (via a new _parse_brex_root helper — needed because a snsRules-only BREX can have zero content rules, so _get_object_rule_nodes's node list can't be relied on to reach the tree) and reports DuplicateSnsCode when two sibling elements at the same level (grouped by parent) share an snsCode text value, MissingSnsTitle when a level element has no snsTitle child, and SnsCodeOutsidePattern when a snsCode fails every valueForm="pattern" content rule declared elsewhere in the same file for the corresponding dmCode attribute (snsSystem -> @systemCode, snsSubSystem -> @subSystemCode, snsSubSubSystem -> @subSubSystemCode, snsAssy -> @assyCode, matched by a rule's objectPath/objpath ending in that attribute name — a heuristic name match, since nothing in the schema formally links an snsRules level to a content rule; skipped when no such pattern rule exists for that attribute at all, since there is nothing to check against). Reuses the objectPath nodes lint_brex already selected (passed in as content_rule_nodes) to build the pattern cross-reference without a second selection pass, and the same translate_xsd_regex_to_python/regex V1 compilation lint_brex's own InvalidPattern check uses, skipping a pattern that doesn't itself compile (already reported separately by that check). Verified against the real evidence-base ATABREX (DMC-ATABREX-...-01A..., the one with 749 real SNS codes across snsSystem(78)/snsSubSystem(391)/snsSubSubSystem(280)): zero findings, confirming none of the three checks false-positive at scale against a large, real, well-formed SNS table; the 7 bundled default BREX (acd/brex/*.XML) declare no snsRules at all, so the check is a no-op on those, as expected. Covered by tests/test_brex_lint.py: duplicate snsCode among siblings reported with both lines, distinct codes not flagged, a missing snsTitle reported, a present snsTitle not flagged, a snsCode outside its declared pattern reported, a matching snsCode not flagged, no flag when no pattern rule is declared for that attribute at all, and a BREX with no snsRules producing none of the three finding categories.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: objectUse read as full text content; a missing objectUse is tolerated
tasks.details: Read objectUse as full text content (''.join(node.itertext())) instead of .text, and tolerate a missing objectUse instead of raising IndexError. Ref §3.12, category D4. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _show_rules now reads x.getparent().xpath('objectUse|objuse'), joining itertext() of the first match instead of taking .text (which silently dropped any content after a child element), and stores None instead of raising IndexError when a rule has no objectUse/objuse at all (the shape lint_brex's pre-existing MissingObjectUse finding already flags statically). Covered by tests/test_p3_robustness_hygiene.py: an objectUse with inline child markup reads as its full joined text, and a rule with no objectUse reports Description: None instead of raising.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: Each BREX parsed once per run and its rule list cached
tasks.details: Parse each BREX once per run, not once per data module, and cache the extracted rule list. Ref §3.12. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py as BrexChecker._get_content_rules(brex, schema, debug), a cached wrapper around _show_rules keyed by (brex, schema) on a new self._rule_cache dict (cleared only on a fresh BrexChecker instance, since a BREX file's content doesn't change mid-run and repeated instantiation across different runs already gets a fresh cache). _check_rules's per-document loop now calls _get_content_rules instead of _show_rules directly, so a BREX is parsed and its rule list extracted once per (brex, schema) pair for the life of the checker instance rather than once per document — directory-mode validate() and repeated single-object validate() calls against the same BREX chain both benefit. Covered by tests/test_p3_robustness_hygiene.py: _get_object_rule_nodes (the actual parse) spied across three documents checked against the same BREX and schema, asserting exactly one call, plus _get_content_rules returning the identical cached list object across calls.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: Each objectPath compiled once and reused across documents
tasks.details: Compile each objectPath once into a reusable selector and evaluate it against each document, instead of recompiling per (rule, document). Ref §3.12. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: _show_rules compiles elementpath.Selector(xpath, namespaces=...) once per rule when the rule dict is built (piggybacking on the _get_content_rules cache above so it truly happens once per (brex, schema) pair, not once per document), storing the compiled selector as value['selector'] (None plus a captured value['selector_error'] on a compile failure, instead of raising immediately). _check_object_flag_0/1/2 no longer construct their own elementpath.Selector; a new shared _resolve_selector(brex_violations, value) helper returns the precompiled selector or records an xpathError from the captured compile failure. Evaluation itself (_select_with_nodes(selector, root)) still runs fresh per document via its own elementpath.XPathContext, and is still wrapped in try/except elementpath.ElementPathError per call since a dynamic (evaluation-time) error can depend on the specific document, not just the rule. Covered by tests/test_p3_robustness_hygiene.py: a rule's selector is an elementpath.Selector instance and is the identical object across repeated _get_content_rules calls, and a rule with an unparseable objectPath reports a single xpathError (no exception) with no recompilation attempt.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: regex_builder escapes attribute names and values
tasks.details: Escape attribute values in regex_builder (regex.escape), or drop the raw-text search entirely once line numbers come from the parsed tree. Ref §3.12. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: regex_builder now escapes both attribute_name and attribute_value with regex.escape before embedding them in the built pattern, so a value containing regex metacharacters (., (, [, …) is matched literally instead of producing a wrong or invalid pattern. Covered by tests/test_p3_robustness_hygiene.py: an attribute value containing ./(/) matches only its literal text and not an unrelated string that would incidentally satisfy the unescaped pattern, and likewise for an attribute name containing a metacharacter.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: Saxon path removed (product decision); elementpath is the only engine
tasks.details: Make the Saxon path complete or remove it — it is only wired into _check_object_flag_0, so saxon=True currently gives an inconsistent mix of engines. Ref §3.12. Per explicit product decision, removed rather than completed: the Saxon branch had zero test coverage and completing it would have meant duplicating _check_object_flag_1/_check_object_flag_2/_check_object_values/node-xpath-and-copy/line-number/rule-hit-statistics logic against the Saxon API for no behavioural gain over the existing elementpath path. Removed the saxonche import, the saxon constructor parameter and self._saxon attribute, the Saxon branch of _check_object_flag_0 (and its now-unused xml_text parameter/plumbing through _check_rules), and the saxonche line from requirements.txt; clean_xpath (only ever called from the removed branch) is kept since it remains part of the package's public API (acd/__init__.py). Covered by tests/test_p3_robustness_hygiene.py: BrexChecker(saxon=True) raises TypeError and a plain BrexChecker() instance carries no _saxon attribute; the full existing suite (acd/brex_checker.py imports and 246 tests) passes with no saxonche installed.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: XPath version chosen like s1kd: 1.0 for S1000D <= 3.0 BREX, 2.0 for 4.0+
tasks.details: Select the XPath version the way s1kd does: XPath 1.0 for BREX declaring S1000D <= 3.0, XPath 2.0 for 4.0+, with an explicit override. Ours is always XPath 2.0 — correct for these BREX, wrong for a 3.0 BREX that relies on XPath 1.0 =-on-node-set semantics. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: set_xpath_version(version) is the -X/--xpath-version equivalent ("1.0"/"2.0"/None for dynamic, validated against the new XPATH_VERSIONS constant), and _brex_requires_xpath2(brex_schema) ports brex_requires_xpath2 (s1kd-brexcheck.c:1296-1322): an explicit override always wins; otherwise a BREX declaring S1000D issue 2.0/2.1/2.2/2.3/3.0 (_XPATH1_ONLY_ISSUE_PREFIXES) gets elementpath.XPath1Parser, everything else (4.0+, or no/unrecognised xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation) gets elementpath.XPath2Parser -- the existing default. The decision is made once per BREX file in _show_rules (from the BREX's own root xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation, read via the same nodes_to_check[0].getroottree().getroot() the existing defaultBrSeverityLevel lookup already uses -- moot when a BREX has no rules to compile a selector for), not from the checked object's schema, matching the C original's xmlDocGetRootElement(brex) rather than the dmod being checked; the chosen parser is passed to every elementpath.Selector(...) compiled from that BREX. lint_brex's independent InvalidXPath compile check is updated the same way, so a lint result reflects the version real checking would actually use for that BREX. Verified against all 7 bundled default BREX (acd/brex/*.XML): the S1000D <= 3.0 one (DMC-AE-A-...) selects XPath 1.0, the six 4.x ones (issues A/D/E/F/G/H) select XPath 2.0, zero compile failures across all of them; the real evidence-base ATABREX pair (both declaring S1000D 4.2) also continues to select XPath 2.0 unchanged. Covered by tests/test_xpath_version.py: dynamic XPath 1.0 for every legacy issue (2.0/2.1/2.2/2.3/3.0) and XPath 2.0 for 4.2 and for an undeclared schema, a concrete pass/fail difference using the XPath-2.0-only matches() function (fails to compile under dynamic mode for a 3.0-declared BREX, compiles for a 4.2-declared one), the explicit override forcing either version regardless of declared issue, set_xpath_version(None) restoring dynamic selection, rejection of an unsupported version string, lint_brex's InvalidXPath finding tracking the same dynamic decision, and an end-to-end _check_rules() run recording an xpathError for the incompatible rule while the BREX's other, XPath-1-compatible rule is unaffected.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: Directory filter uses a real extension test; BREX data modules are checked too
tasks.details:
Replace the ".xml" in name / "-022a-" not in name directory filter with a real extension test, and check BREX data modules like any other object. Ref §3.11. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: validate()'s directory-mode file filter is now _.lower().endswith(".xml") and isfile(join(self._xml_dir, _)) (matching the extension-test convention already used by s1000d.collect_csdb_schemas/find_document_by_reference), dropping both the substring extension test and the -022a- exclusion entirely, so a BREX data module sitting in the checked directory is listed and checked exactly like any other object.

Removing the exclusion surfaced a real, previously-unreachable consequence: a self-referencing master/default BREX (the standard shape for a top-level BREX with nothing above it -- confirmed on the real bundled DMC-S1000D-F-... default BREX and reproduced against the real evidence-base CSDB) checked directly as the primary object hit _walk_brex_chain's existing cycle guard on its very first lookup (its own brexDmRef resolves to itself), which returned an empty chain and made _init_brex_list raise NoBrexDefined for every such file -- i.e. BREX data modules could be listed but not actually checked. Fixed in _walk_brex_chain: when the self-reference terminates the walk on its first iteration (xml == xml_start), the file is appended as its own sole applicable BREX instead of yielding an empty chain, mirroring s1kd's main() (strcmp(brex_fnames[0], dmod_fnames[i]) == 0), where find_brex_fname_from_doc already resolves such a reference to the file itself. A self-reference reached deeper in the walk (a referenced BREX's own terminating self-reference, the pre-existing and already-tested case) is unaffected, since that BREX is already in the list from the previous iteration. Verified end-to-end against the real evidence-base CSDB (CMP 21-77-05): directory-mode validate() now checks all 3 BREX files it contains (previously always excluded) without raising -- the two ATABREX layers resolve their normal chain and report 0 errors, and the self-referencing S1000D 4.2 default BREX checks against itself and reports one real SNS finding (its own systemCode against its own declared SNS rules) rather than crashing; lint_brex_layers on a self-referencing BREX passed directly (unaffected code path, verified against the same bundled default BREX) still correctly reports no findings. Covered by tests/test_directory_mode.py (real extension test rejecting foo.xml.bak, case-insensitive .XML matching, a directory literally named weird.xml ignored, a -022a--named data module now checked and flagged) and tests/test_brex_dm_ref_resolution.py (_init_brex_list resolving a self-referencing BREX checked directly to itself, and an end-to-end validate() run against it raising nothing).

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: Structured violation objects (dataclass) returned
tasks.details: Return structured violation objects (dataclass: brex, rule id, brDecisionIdentNumber, flag, severity, objectPath, objectUse, allowed values, node xpath, line, node snippet) instead of nested dicts keyed by integers, and derive the JSON and XML reports from them. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: a new @dataclass BrexViolation (document, brex, rule_id, br_decision_ident_number, flag, rules_context, severity, fail, object_path, object_use, allowed_values, node_xpath, line, node_snippet, duplicate) is the canonical structured shape a violation is reported in. _check_rules's per-BREX result[brex_path]['0'/'1'/'2'] dict lists (kept unchanged -- existing callers and the whole test suite key off them directly, and s1kd-brexcheck's own shape is dict-based) now also carry 'RuleId' (structureObjectRule/objrule @id, newly captured in _show_rules) and 'RulesContext' alongside the fields already there. _violation_from_dict(document, brex, flag, violation) is the single conversion point from a raw record to a BrexViolation; violations(result) flattens an entire validate()/_check_rules() result (single-object or directory-mode, via _is_single_object_result) through it into one ordered list. Both report formats are derived from that same conversion rather than each walking the raw dicts independently: to_xml_report's _append_error_node now takes a BrexViolation (reading its typed attributes instead of dict keys) and _build_document_node builds one via _violation_from_dict before calling it; the new to_json_report(result, indent=2) returns {"summary": run_summary(result), "violations": [...]} with each violation as BrexViolation.to_dict() (dataclasses.asdict), replacing the "ad-hoc JSON" category D6 originally flagged (dump(result, ...) of the raw internal dict) with a defined, typed shape. BrexViolation is exported from acd/__init__.py. Covered by tests/test_structured_violations.py.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: Identical violations from layered BREX deduplicated
tasks.details: Deduplicate identical violations raised by the same rule appearing in multiple layered BREX. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py as BrexChecker._deduplicate_violations, called once at the end of _check_rules over the finished brex_violations_dict. Layered BREX commonly re-states or inherits the same rule verbatim across layers (a project BREX re-declaring, or simply not overriding, a rule its master BREX already defines); checking the object against every layer in the chain then produces one violation record per layer for what is really a single real-world defect. Two violations are treated as the same when they share (flag, RulesContext, Xpath, NodeXpath) -- the same "same rule" definition lint_brex_layers already established (rulesContext/context + exact objectPath/objpath text), plus landing on the same node (or both having no backing node at all, e.g. two layers' identical flag-1 "required but missing" result, which is still the same violation). self._brex_list[0] is walked in its existing project-specific-layer-first order (see _walk_brex_chain/lint_brex_layers's "layer 0 is the lower, project-specific BREX" convention), so the first-seen copy -- the more specific layer's -- is left as canonical and every later copy is marked 'Duplicate': True; nothing is removed from result[brex_path]['0'/'1'/'2'], so its length and per-BREX keying are unchanged and every existing caller/test that indexes it directly is unaffected. _count_violations (and therefore _append_summary/run_summary) and to_xml_report/to_json_report (via BrexViolation.duplicate) all skip a Duplicate: True entry, so error/warning counts and both report formats reflect the deduplicated set while the raw dict keeps every record for transparency. The identity key intentionally omits Brex, so two literal duplicate rule definitions within a *single* BREX file are deduplicated the same way. Covered by tests/test_structured_violations.py: raw per-layer records both present with only the later one marked duplicate, _append_summary/run_summary/to_json_report/to_xml_report all counting the pair once, and a same-file duplicate-rule case.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: Progress callback replaces the tqdm dependency
tasks.details: Add a progress callback rather than the hard tqdm dependency inside the library. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py: removed from tqdm import tqdm and the include_tqdm bool parameter entirely (no prior test coverage depended on it), replacing both call sites -- _check_rules's per-content-rule loop and validate()'s directory-mode per-file loop -- with a single progress_callback: Callable[[int, int, str], None] = None parameter, called as progress_callback(current, total, stage) with stage="rules" or stage="files" respectively (validate() forwards its own progress_callback into _check_rules, so both stages surface through one callback). None (the default) reports nothing, preserving prior behaviour exactly for every existing caller. A caller who wants a tqdm bar (or any other progress UI/logging) now drives it themselves from the callback, e.g. lambda current, total, stage: bars[stage].update(1); acd/brex_checker.py itself no longer imports tqdm at all. tqdm is left in requirements.txt and untouched elsewhere in the package (acd/filelist.py, acd/copying.py still use their own unrelated include_tqdm parameters), since only this file's hard dependency was in scope. Covered by tests/test_progress_callback.py: the module carries no tqdm attribute, _check_rules reports (current, total, "rules") once per content rule, validate() reports (current, total, "files") once per file in directory mode, and omitting the callback still works.

tasks.group: 4.4 P3 — Improvements to checks we already perform
tasks.short: Opt-in clear error for objects without xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation
tasks.details: Raise a clear error when the object has no xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation (DTD-based objects) instead of comparing rulesContext against None. Implemented as an opt-in setting rather than an unconditional raise: a genuine S1000D <= 3.0 / DTD-based object legitimately has no xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation at all (that mechanism is XSD-only), and _check_rules already handles that case correctly today -- schema resolves to None, every schema-qualified contextRules/rulesContext group is skipped and every unqualified one still applies, exactly as tests/test_legacy_brex_spellings.py's test_legacy_context_qualified_rule_skipped_for_non_matching_schema (a schema-less object, by design) already verifies; s1kd-brexcheck itself never errors on a missing schema either (xmlGetNsProp returns NULL silently, s1kd-brexcheck.c:1371). Raising unconditionally would have broken exactly the legacy-spelling support added earlier in this list. Implemented in acd/brex_checker.py as a new NoSchemaDeclared exception (exported from acd/__init__.py) plus BrexChecker.set_require_schema(enabled=True) (off by default, matching every other opt-in checker setting in this codebase -- set_ignore_empty, set_xpath_version, etc.): when enabled, _check_rules raises NoSchemaDeclared immediately after get_schema_from_xml resolves to None, with a message naming the checked object and explaining both why (schema-qualified rules cannot be selected) and the escape hatch (set_require_schema(False), the default, for a genuine DTD-based object). Intended for a caller checking a corpus of objects that are all expected to be XSD/4.0+-based, where a missing declaration on one of them is far more likely an authoring mistake than a legitimate legacy object, and silently under-checking it would hide that mistake instead of surfacing it. Covered by tests/test_no_schema_declared.py: default behaviour unchanged (no raise) for a schema-less object, the option raising for one, the option not firing when a schema is declared, toggling the option back off, the option defaulting to off on a fresh checker, and the raise surfacing through validate() too.

tasks.group: 4.5 P4 — Test suite

tasks.group: 4.5 P4 — Test suite
tasks.short: Fixtures for each allowedObjectFlag across node-set, boolean, string, numeric results
tasks.details: Add fixtures for each allowedObjectFlag covering node-set, boolean, string and numeric XPath results. Implemented as tests/test_allowed_object_flag_result_types.py, exercising _check_object_flag_0/1/2 directly against //foo (node-set), //foo = 'bar' (boolean), string(...) and count(...) (scalar string/number) for flags 0 and 1, plus the flag-2 value-check equivalents. Writing this fixture surfaced two previously-undiscovered defects of the same class §3.2 already fixed for booleans, now also fixed in acd/brex_checker.py: _check_object_flag_0 crashed with TypeError: object of type 'int' has no len() on a bare numeric objectPath (e.g. count(...), since neither 0 nor 1 has a len()) and silently miscounted a bare string result by iterating over its characters instead of treating it as one result (string(//foo) evaluating to "bar" produced 3 bogus violations, one per character); _check_object_flag_2 had the identical bug (crash on a number passed to _check_object_values's enumerate, per-character iteration on a string) in its value-checking path. Both now treat any scalar XPath result (boolean, string, number, Decimal) as a single result -- flag 0 via isinstance(result, (bool, str, int, float, Decimal)) evaluated for truthiness (matching how _check_object_flag_1 already handled these types), flag 2 by wrapping a scalar result as the sole item of a one-element list before value-checking. Flag 0's new placeholder line label "(Scalar condition -> Interpret XPath)" sits alongside the existing "(Boolean condition -> Interpret XPath)", unchanged for an actual boolean result so no prior test's exact string assertion could break (verified none existed either way). Full pre-existing suite (286 tests) still passes unchanged.

tasks.group: 4.5 P4 — Test suite
tasks.short: SNS fixture: normal, strict and unstrict modes against the real ATABREX 01A

tasks.details: Add a layered-BREX fixture (DM → ATABREX 01A → ATABREX 00A → S1000D default) asserting all layers are collected exactly once, plus a cyclic-reference fixture. Implemented as tests/test_evidence_layered_brex_chain.py, walking the real chain named in the §4.2 "Use brexDmRef for BREX resolution" task note above (DMC-CTTAE29N-A-00-00-00-01A-00KA-D -> both real ATABREX layers -> the real DMC-S1000D-F-04-10-0301-00A-022A-D default BREX -- which, unlike assumed while drafting this fixture, is itself physically present in the evidence folder alongside the two ATABREX files, since all three are the same BREX the plan's whole §1 evidence base was built from, so this chain resolves entirely from real on-disk files with no built-in-default fallback involved; test_default_brex.py already covers that fallback path directly with our bundled acd/brex/ copies). tasks.group: 4.5 P4 — Test suite

tasks.group: 4.5 P4 — Test suite
tasks.short: Differential harness against s1kd-brexcheck -clnST over CMP 21-77-05
tasks.details: Add a differential harness that runs both brex_checker.py and s1kd-brexcheck -clnST over the whole CMP 21-77-05 folder and diffs the violation sets, so parity is measurable and intentional divergences are recorded. Implemented as tests/differential_harness.py (the parsing/diffing logic -- not itself a test_*.py module, so pytest does not try to collect it directly) plus tests/test_differential_harness.py. Both tools can emit an XML report in the same brexCheck shape (to_xml_report, category D6, was deliberately built compatible with s1kd-brexcheck -x's documented shape from its man page); parse_brex_check_xml_report is the single parser used for both sides, normalizing s1kd's "one <error>, several <object> children" grouping and our "one violation record per <error>" shape into the same flat per-node representation before comparison. run_s1kd_brexcheck runs the checklist's literal -c -l -n -S -T, plus -x (report format only -- changes nothing about what is checked, needed to get a diffable structured report at all). diff_violation_sets compares by (brex, document, flag, objectPath) basename-normalized keys (deliberately excluding line/node-xpath, which the two independently-implemented engines are not expected to format identically) and classifies a rule using matches()/tokenize()/lower-case() as an intentional, documented divergence (§1: 6 of 919 real rules use these, uncompilable under a default XPath-1-only s1kd build) rather than a real gap; ParsedViolation.key(include_brex=False) is available for the case where a built-in-default-BREX fallback layer ends up labelled differently by the two tools. The parsing/diffing logic is fully unit-tested with no external binary needed, including a round-trip through our own real to_xml_report output (10/10 passing). The actual cross-tool run (test_differential_parity_over_the_evidence_folder) additionally needs a real s1kd-brexcheck build, which this environment does not have -- no prebuilt binary on PATH, and building it needs libxml2/libxslt/libexslt development headers the available MSYS2/mingw64 toolchain does not have installed (confirmed via pkg-config; see s1kd-tools-master/tools/s1kd-brexcheck/Makefile) -- so it is skipped rather than faked (verified skipping cleanly), and is designed to actually run wherever both the binary (S1KD_BREXCHECK_BIN) and the evidence folder (ACD_BREX_EVIDENCE_DIR) are available.

tasks.short: Decimal XPath results handled in _check_object_flag_1 (crash fix)
tasks.details: Handle Decimal XPath results in _check_object_flag_1 (CRASH). §4.5's "fixtures for each allowedObjectFlag" item fixed scalar-result handling in _check_object_flag_0 (isinstance(result, (bool, str, int, float, Decimal))) and _check_object_flag_2 (same tuple minus bool), but _check_object_flag_1 was left at isinstance(result, (str, int, float)). elementpath returns decimal.Decimal — not float — for any XPath arithmetic or decimal literal (count(//b) div 4, count(//b) + 0.5, 1.5), so such a result falls through to the node-set branch and raises TypeError: object of type 'decimal.Decimal' has no len(), aborting the whole run.
