tasks.group: 4.6 P0/P1 — Rework found by auditing §4.1–§4.5 against the evidence base
tasks.short: Removed the obsolete and-in-XPath line-number heuristics
tasks.details:
Remove the two obsolete and-in-XPath line-number heuristics, which discard the real line numbers §4.4 added. _check_object_flag_0 (if ' and ' in value['xpath']) and _check_object_values substitute a placeholder string — "(Origin traced back to multiple lines -> Interpret XPath)" / "... -> Read XPath)" — for Line whenever the objectPath contains and. That predates §4.4's "Report the violating node's real line number", which made _node_line_number(node) resolve the exact violating node: violations are now one-per-node, so there is nothing ambiguous left to hedge about. Measured impact: 148 of the 919 real rules (16%) contain ' and ', all of them flag 0, and on a full directory-mode run over the real CMP 21-77-05 corpus both flag-0 violations found report the placeholder instead of a line number. Reproduced minimally with //bad[@x and @y] against a document with two bad elements: NodeXpath correctly resolves /dmodule[1]/bad[1] and /dmodule[1]/bad[2], proving the nodes — and therefore their real lines, 4 and 6 — are known, while both records report the placeholder string. Fix: delete both heuristics and always use _node_line_number(node), keeping "x" only for a violation with no backing node.

While removing it, note that _check_object_values's guard is also broken on its own terms: if (r'] and ' or r'and \[' or r'] and \[' or ...) in value['xpath'] is an or-chain of non-empty string literals, which Python collapses to its first operand, so the test is only ever '] and ' in value['xpath'] — the other five alternatives (and their stray regex escaping, in what is a plain substring test) have never had any effect. Both problems disappear with the heuristic.

tasks.group: 4.6 P0/P1 — Rework found by auditing §4.1–§4.5 against the evidence base
tasks.short: SNS and notation checks gated behind opt-in check_sns / check_notations (default off)
tasks.details:
Gate SNS and notation-rule checking behind opt-in parameters, matching s1kd-brexcheck's -S / -n. §4.2 ported both checks faithfully but wired them into _check_rules unconditionally; in the C original opts->check_sns and opts->check_notations both default to false (s1kd-brexcheck.c:1994, :2084, :2091) and gate the calls at :1376 and :1383. There is currently no way to turn either off. Measured impact on the real CMP 21-77-05 corpus (67 objects): 59 SNS + 32 notation violations are reported by default, all counted as errors by _append_summary/run_summary, where a default s1kd-brexcheck invocation reports none.

The 59 SNS findings are genuine and correctly ported — verified by hand: the ATABREX declares snsSystem 21 → snsSubSystem 7 with no snsSubSubSystem children at all, and should_check does check a non-placeholder subSubSystemCode — they are simply not something the reference tool surfaces unasked. The 32 notation findings are worse: no BREX in the resolved chain declares a single notationRule (confirmed: notationRuleList count is 0 in all three), and check_entity's logic reports every unparsed entity as disallowed when the merged rule group is empty. tests/test_notation_rules.py::test_no_notation_rules_defined_reports_with_generic_description pins that behaviour today, and it is a faithful port — but it is only defensible because the C tool never reaches it without -n.

Fix: add check_sns: bool and check_notations: bool parameters to validate()/_check_rules() and gate the two calls. Decide and record the default explicitly: matching the C original means defaulting both to False (and updating the existing SNS/notation tests to opt in), while defaulting to True preserves today's output but needs the empty-rule-group short-circuit for notations, to avoid flagging every entity in a CSDB whose BREX chain constrains no notations.

Fixed. validate() and _check_rules() both take check_sns: bool = False and check_notations: bool = False, gating the _check_sns_rules and _check_notation_rules calls in _check_rules. The default is False for both, matching the C original — a plain validate() now reports what a plain s1kd-brexcheck invocation reports, and the 59 SNS + 32 notation findings on CMP 21-77-05 are only produced when explicitly asked for. Consequently the empty-rule-group short-circuit for notations was *not* added: reporting every unparsed entity when the BREX chain declares no notationRule stays a faithful port of check_entity, and is only reachable under the explicit opt-in, exactly as in the C tool. When a check is off its key is absent from the result entirely (not an empty list), which every consumer already handles — _count_violations skips missing keys, and to_xml_report/_append_sns_notation_nodes already reads them with result.get(...), so no <sns>/<notations> node is emitted. sns_mode is unchanged and now only has an effect under check_sns=True.

Tests updated to opt in rather than change what they assert: the _validate helpers in tests/test_sns_rules.py, tests/test_notation_rules.py and tests/test_evidence_sns_real_atabrex.py, the two standalone cases in those files that build their own checker, test_run_summary.py::test_sns_and_notation_violations_counted_as_errors_with_no_severity, and the three to_xml_report cases in tests/test_xml_report.py. tests/test_differential_harness.py::test_differential_parity_over_the_evidence_folder also opts in, since run_s1kd_brexcheck passes -S -n on the other side and the two runs must be checking the same thing. Full suite: 368 passed, 1 skipped.

tasks.short: SNS and notation violations included in to_json_report
tasks.details: Include SNS and notation violations in to_json_report. violations() deliberately covers only content-rule violations (documented — SNS/notation have no objectPath/objectUse/allowed-values shape to fit BrexViolation), and to_xml_report emits them separately via _append_sns_notation_nodes. to_json_report got no equivalent, so its summary and its violations list contradict each other. Reproduced on a real object from CMP 21-77-05: the report reads "summary": {… "Errors": 5 …} alongside "violations": [], with no way for a consumer to learn what the five errors were. Fix: give to_json_report top-level sns and notations keys mirroring the XML report's nodes — and nonContextRules/brexFallback alongside them for parity with to_xml_report — so the JSON report is self-consistent and carries everything the XML report does.

tasks.group: 4.6 P0/P1 — Rework found by auditing §4.1–§4.5 against the evidence base
tasks.short: objectValue without valueForm / valtype treated as single
tasks.details: Treat an objectValue with no @valueForm/@valtype as single. _show_rules dispatches on value_form with if "single" / elif "pattern" / elif "range" and no else, so an objectValue that declares no form has its valueAllowed silently dropped from values_allowed. The C reference does the opposite — check_node_values (s1kd-brexcheck.c:219-248) makes exact string equality the else branch, reached whenever form is NULL — and this plan's own §2.C already specifies "single (or absent) | Exact string equality". Two consequences: a rule whose only objectValue omits the form becomes a silent no-op (all three allowed-value lists stay empty, so _check_rules's has_values gate skips it entirely), and a rule mixing a form-less objectValue with a formed one reports false-positive violations for values the BREX does allow. Latent in the corpus — all 2462 objectValue in the three evidence BREX and all 7 bundled default BREX declare a form (verified) — but @valueForm is optional in the schema. Fix: make single the fallback branch, and add a fixture to tests/test_value_form_matrix.py for a form-less objectValue both alone and mixed with a pattern one.

tasks.group: 4.6 P0/P1 — Rework found by auditing §4.1–§4.5 against the evidence base
tasks.short: Element values compared as full text content, not .text
tasks.details: Compare element values as full text content, not .text. _check_object_values reads an element result as element.text or "", which stops at the first child element; the C reference uses xmlNodeGetContent(node) (s1kd-brexcheck.c:232), the full recursive text. An element with mixed content (<title>Some <emphasis>bold</emphasis> text</title>) is therefore compared as "Some " and reported as violating a rule it satisfies. This is the same defect §4.4 already fixed one level up for objectUse ("Read objectUse as full text content … instead of .text"); the value comparison was missed. Fix: use ''.join(element.itertext()) and add a mixed-content case to tests/test_value_form_matrix.py.
